title: ID0477897-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP/S2 170003301] Charger sequence check
description:
Reported behavior/issue -
Please review the following sequence for charger 170003301 at Galway Retail Park on 11 February 2026 between 09:42 and 10:06 UTC.

additional_info.subject: Brite - 170003301 – 11 Feb 2026 behaviour (09:42–10:06 UTC) + request for deeper visibility
additional_info.body:
Hi Francisco,
Please review the following sequence for charger 170003301 at Galway Retail Park on 11 February 2026 between 09:42 and 10:06 UTC.
Connector 4
09:42:13 UTC
Status: Faulted
VendorErrorCode: “evse is not ready”
09:46:31 UTC
Status: Faulted
ErrorCode: InternalError
Connector 2
09:46:12 UTC
Status: Faulted
ErrorCode: InternalError
This coincided with a manual disconnect and return-to-holster event and appears to have been a brief transient.
Connector 1
10:01:27.579 UTC
Status: Preparing
ErrorCode: NoError
10:02:55.508 UTC
Status: Available
ErrorCode: NoError
In this case, a BYD vehicle was moved between connectors due to difficulty initiating charge. Connector 1 entered Preparing but never transitioned to Charging and returned cleanly to Available without any EVSE fault. The vehicle was then moved back to connector 4, where at 10:05:48 UTC the session started successfully and charged normally.
The chargepoint remained Online and Available at CP level throughout.
From the sequence, connector 1 appears to show a clean negotiation abort, while connector 4 earlier shows readiness/internal fault behaviour before later starting successfully.
Could you please:
Review connector 4 at 09:42–09:47 UTC to confirm what internal readiness condition maps to “evse is not ready” and the subsequent InternalError.
Review connector 1 at 10:01–10:03 UTC to confirm why it exited Preparing without transitioning to Charging (protocol timeout, ISO 15118/DIN negotiation failure, EV abort, authorisation path, etc.).
Confirm whether there is any shared cabinet-level condition that could explain connector 4 readiness faults independent of vehicle negotiation.
Additionally, in cases where we suspect vehicle-side negotiation instability, is there any way for us to access more granular diagnostic information at CPO level? For example, visibility of ISO 15118/DIN state transitions, SLAC results, precharge attempts, contactor commands, or protocol timeouts. At present we only see high-level OCPP state changes, which makes it difficult to determine whether behaviour is vehicle-driven or EVSE-driven without your internal logs.
We would like to understand what level of protocol or hardware diagnostics can be made available to us for future analysis.
Thanks,
Colin

VendorErrorCode
– This issue is related to the connection from EcoG.
